videos.title: Getting started with ChatGPT Work
videos.focus: Choosing Work for multi-step tasks with connected context
videos.summary: OpenAI’s Training walkthrough distinguishes quick conversational work from multi-step tasks that gather context across connected apps. Its worked example shows a user connecting Gmail and Slack, requesting unsubscribe candidates, reviewing proposed actions and approving the result rather than giving an agent unchecked authority.
videos.why_it_matters: Readers can decide when a task warrants Work, connect only the needed sources, request a reviewable proposal and retain approval before consequential actions are completed.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete first-party Training walkthrough, stated eight-minute runtime, embedded video identity, Work-versus-Chat guidance, connected-app example, approval sequence and practice task; no audiovisual playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Decide when a task needs Work, gather bounded context from connected apps and preserve review before consequential actions.
quality_review.practical_action: Choose one scattered information task, connect only its required sources and ask for a reviewable proposal before approving any external action.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected after Academy, YouTube, Microsoft and IBM Mediacenter surfaces failed protected advancement; this first-party Training page exposes a native full-length HTML5 player and substantive written walkthrough.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete walkthrough covering Chat versus Work selection, plugin connections, the Gmail and Slack example, review and approval behavior, a practice prompt, and the next learning step.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: The lesson is product-specific but instructional, with explicit limits, review points and a synthetic practice example rather than a purchase pitch.
transferable_takeaways: Use conversational chat for focused exploration and choose an agentic workspace only when several sources or steps materially help.
Connect the minimum sources required for the task and state the desired reviewable outcome before execution begins.
Inspect proposed changes and preserve an explicit approval step before an assistant performs consequential actions in connected systems.

videos.title: Choose the right AI model for your use case
videos.focus: Model selection criteria and multi-model evaluation
videos.summary: IBM AI Academy presents a compact model-selection framework that compares use-case fit, performance, risk and deployment constraints instead of treating the largest model as the automatic choice.
videos.why_it_matters: Readers can turn the lesson into a short candidate scorecard and test smaller and larger models against the same task before committing budget or infrastructure.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete IBM AI Academy companion lesson, exact runtime, stated evaluation criteria and all three learning objectives; no audiovisual playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Assess candidate AI models against use-case fit, performance, risk and deployment needs rather than defaulting to size.
quality_review.practical_action: Create a one-page scorecard for one workflow, test multiple candidate models on the same examples and document the trade-offs.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected after the original IBM episode failed rotation; this distinct lesson supplies concrete transferable model-evaluation criteria and a publisher player that previously passed duration-matched advancement.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete AI Academy companion lesson covering the multi-model approach, model assessment criteria, performance evaluation, faculty attribution and linked model-selection guidebook.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: IBM links its products and guidebook, but the reviewed lesson teaches a transferable model-selection framework rather than a purchase-focused product announcement.
transferable_takeaways: Start from the use case and desired outcome before comparing model size, benchmark performance or provider claims.
Evaluate candidate models on performance, risk, cost and deployment constraints using the same representative task examples.
Prefer a multi-model portfolio when different workflows require different balances of speed, accuracy, transparency and operating cost.

podcasts.title: Tool Integration Triggers Severe Safety Refusal Degradation
podcasts.summary: This complete transcript reviews evidence that tool access changes agent safety behavior, then connects monitoring limits, capability boundaries, policy and evaluation fragility into a compact governance briefing.
podcasts.why_it_matters: Readers can translate the episode into a test plan that evaluates prompts, tools, permissions and monitoring together instead of assuming model-only safety transfers unchanged.

verification.content_review_basis: Read the complete publisher transcript from disclosure through the final governance and evaluation conclusions; no audio-playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Understand why tool-enabled agents require joint evaluation of model behavior, permissions, monitor inputs and downstream effects.
quality_review.practical_action: Add tool access to one safety test, record changed refusal behavior and verify permission boundaries and monitor inputs before deployment.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected because the exact episode supplies a complete transcript and stays entirely focused on AI safety and governance.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the entire 3:57 transcript, including tool-triggered refusal changes, transcript-monitor evasion, capability controls, policy, certification and benchmark sensitivity.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: The transcript contains a brief follow request but no paid sponsor segment or product-purchase pitch within the editorial discussion.

editorial_segments.topic: Tool-enabled agent safety failures, monitoring limits, capability controls, policy and evaluation fragility

podcasts.title: AI in the AM: Where’s the Steering Wheel?
podcasts.summary: The full transcript examines control over connected agents, evaluation-aware models, hidden internal signals, formal verification, training data provenance and adoption trust, with clearly marked sponsor breaks.
podcasts.why_it_matters: Readers can compare several control layers and extract a practical rule: preserve human steering, fallback access and verifiable evidence as agents gain more operational authority.

verification.content_review_basis: Read the complete publisher transcript, chapter map and sponsor markers through the recorded 1:25:09 endpoint; no audio-playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Compare technical and organizational controls that preserve human authority as agents receive access to consequential systems.
quality_review.practical_action: Inventory the operational levers an agent can change, then document manual fallback access, evidence requirements and intervention checkpoints.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected for its complete timecoded transcript, multiple substantive expert segments and clear advertisement boundaries from a distinct program.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete 1:25:09 transcript and chapters covering agent control, evaluation awareness, hidden valence, formal verification, data provenance, adoption trust and manual fallback.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: Three sponsor reads are explicitly separated and excluded from the editorial AI denominator; the remaining program is substantive AI discussion.

editorial_segments.topic: Agent access, operational control and evaluation-aware model behavior
Paid sponsor messages for Parallel and OutSystems services
Evaluation awareness and hidden valence research with limitations

Formal verification, training data provenance, model trust, adoption and retained human steering
